## 🎯 Main Idea
- Teaches how to document a penetration test and deliver a professional report — the actual product the client pays for.
- Covers notetaking/evidence handling during the engagement, report types, report structure, writing findings, and reporting workflow/tips.
- Goal: communicate risk clearly to both executive and technical audiences with reproducible, actionable findings.

## 💥 Key Phases & Report Components

### Notetaking & Organization (during the engagement)
- Keep a consistent note structure; log everything for reproducibility and attribution.
- **Key points**
  - Notetaking tools — Obsidian, CherryTree, OneNote; sample structured layout
  - Logging — record all exploitation attempts, commands, and timestamps (tmux logging)
  - Artifacts left behind — track account creation / system modifications for cleanup
  - Evidence — what to capture (screenshots, command output) and how to store it securely
  - Formatting & redaction — blur/blank out passwords; redact sensitive data in screenshots & terminal
  - What NOT to archive — avoid retaining client-sensitive data beyond scope/policy

### Types of Reports
- Report content and depth vary by assessment type and audience.
- **Key points**
  - Vulnerability Assessment vs Penetration Test; Internal vs External scope
  - Inter-disciplinary: Purple Team, Cloud-focused, IoT, Web App, Hardware testing
  - Draft Report → Final Report → Post-Remediation (retest) Report
  - Attestation Report (compliance proof)
  - Other deliverables — slide deck, spreadsheet of findings
  - Vulnerability Notifications — when to draft (critical/urgent issues) and their contents

### Components of a Report
- The standard structure of a professional penetration test report.
- **Key points**
  - Prioritizing efforts — focus on highest-impact issues
  - Attack Chain — narrative walk-through of how compromise was achieved (with reproduction steps)
  - Executive Summary — non-technical, risk-focused; Do/Don't and vocabulary guidance
  - Summary of Recommendations — strategic remediation themes
  - Findings — detailed technical issues
  - Static Appendices — Scope, Methodology, Severity Ratings, Biographies
  - Dynamic Appendices — Exploitation Attempts/Payloads, Compromised Credentials, Config Changes, Additional Affected Scope, Information Gathering, Domain Password Analysis

### How to Write Up a Finding
- Each finding must be clear, reproducible, and actionable.
- **Key points**
  - Breakdown of a finding — description, impact, affected assets, severity, evidence
  - Adequate reproduction steps — enough detail for the client to replicate
  - Effective remediation recommendations — specific, prioritized, with rationale
  - Quality references — authoritative sources (vendor docs, CVEs, standards)
  - Good vs poorly written finding examples (e.g. Kerberoasting, Tomcat default creds)

### Reporting Tips & Tricks (workflow)
- Make reporting efficient, consistent, and high quality.
- **Key points**
  - Templates and MS Word tips & tricks
  - Automation and a reporting tool / findings database
  - Client communication throughout the engagement
  - QA process / report review meeting before delivery
  - Presenting the final product professionally

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- Obsidian / CherryTree / OneNote — structured notetaking
- tmux logging — capture terminal evidence
- Findings database & reporting tools — reuse and consistency
- Severity ratings (CVSS) & methodology sections
- Executive vs technical audience targeting
